title: Etchmiadzin Cathedral, Vagharshapat
summary: Etchmiadzin Cathedral in Vagharshapat, Armenia, is traditionally dated to 301–303, when Gregory the Illuminator had a church built on an earlier temple site. Vahan Mamikonian rebuilt the main part of the present structure in 483–484. A belfry was added in the 17th century and a museum building in 1869.

uncertainty.note: AUA gives 301–303 for the first church and 483/4 for the main part of the present structure; the World History Encyclopedia gives c. 303 and c. 483. End is the present.

as_recorded.value: The main part of the current structure was built by Vahan Mamikonian in 483/4
Construction of Etchmiadzin Cathedral began around c. 303 CE

where.historical_name: Mother cathedral of the Armenian Church, Vagharshapat, Armenia

importance.justification: AUA and the World History Encyclopedia both describe the cathedral as founded in the time of Gregory the Illuminator and as the mother church of the Armenian Church.

reviewer_note: No model: AUA gives external plan 22.55 x 20.72 m with no height; the World History Encyclopedia gives 33 m x 30 m and a height of over 20 m. The two plans disagree and the only height is a lower bound from a reference site, so I drew none. The Wikipedia dome height of 34 m was not used. UNESCO pages returned 403.
